paper_title: Text Generation with Diffusion Language Models A Pre-training Approach   with Continuous Paragraph Denoise
caption: Effect of different diffusion steps on text generation quality, on XSum. The result is the optimal value of 5 Gaussian samples.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of varying diffusion steps on the quality of text generation, specifically for the XSum dataset. The horizontal axis, labeled “Diffusion Step,” displays a linear scale ranging from 0.1 to 2000, with tick marks spaced approximately every 500 units. The vertical axis, labeled “Score,” extends from 0.1 to 41.2, using a logarithmic scale with tick marks appearing at intervals of approximately 10 units. There are four bars, each representing a different ‘ROUGE’ variant: ‘ROUGE-1’ is depicted as a light orange bar with a height of approximately 38.3, ‘ROUGE-2’ is represented by a dark orange bar reaching a height of approximately 41.2, ‘ROUGE-L’ is displayed as a light blue bar with a height of approximately 33.4, and ‘ROUGE-4’ is represented by a dark blue bar with a height of approximately 19.1. The bars are sorted in descending order based on their height, with ‘ROUGE-2’ exhibiting the highest score and ‘ROUGE-4’ having the lowest observed score. No bars are visually emphasized, and the chart presents a clear representation of the score values for each diffusion step variant.
